title: 5 Rules for Better Dropdowns
summary: This lesson outlines five essential rules for designing functional and accessible dropdown menus. It covers touch target sizes, viewport-aware positioning, keyboard accessibility, search functionality for long lists, and optimal animation speeds.

transcript.text: Rule 1: Make the trigger obvious. A caret arrow, a hover state, and a minimum 44 pixel click target.
Users should never wonder if it is clickable.
Rule 2: Flip on edge. When the drop-down hits the viewport bottom, it opens upward.
Never clip the last item off the screen.
Rule 3: Keyboard navigation is not optional. Arrow keys to move, enter to select, escape to close.
Every user deserves access. Every time.
Rule 4: Past 10 items, add search. Filtering beats scrolling every single time.
Rule 5: Animate in under 150 milliseconds. Fast enough to feel instant, slow enough to feel smooth.
Save this before your next dropdown. Follow for more UI systems.

on_screen_text: BEFORE: 30px height (too small), Low contrast border, No hover feedback
AFTER: 44px touch target, Clear caret icon, Hover state feedback
Detect edge. Flip the menu up.
Too fast, Just right, Too slow
Fast to feel instant. Smooth to feel real.
before_after: A small, low-contrast dropdown without a caret (Before) is transformed into a larger, high-contrast dropdown with a clear caret icon and hover feedback (After).
